failureMessage: a hardcoded version+build copy can disagree with the DMG it actually shipped in — the ambiguity that stalled diagnosing the installTap crash (#61/#74/#75)

matchLines.what: a hardcoded `v<version> (<build>)`-shaped string literal outside AppDelegate.swift
matchLines.fix: derive it from Bundle.main.infoDictionary (CFBundleShortVersionString / CFBundleVersion), as AppDelegate.versionLabel does, instead of writing a second copy that can drift from what actually shipped

failureMessage: constructing an engine opens the default input and churns a hidden coreaudiod aggregate device — the one mechanism by which this app could plausibly wedge a mic

matchLines.fix: ask AudioDiagnostics instead — hasUsableInput and inputAvailability answer from HAL queries that open no device; if capture is needed, route it through AudioHub, the engine's single owner

failureMessage: the product's headline promise is that the room's audio never leaves the machine — a client in the capture path is how that promise breaks
fix: keep analysis on-device — drop the client; the app has no accepted egress, so adding one is a product decision that belongs in RULES.md first

matchLines.what: the Network framework imported in the capture path

failureMessage: the product promise is that only derived metadata is kept and no audio is stored — a file-writing audio API in the capture path is how that promise breaks
fix: keep audio out of persistence — drop the writer; deliberately adding audio storage (the v3 roadmap) is a product decision that belongs in RULES.md and the mic usage strings first

failureMessage: AudioDiagnostics is the only thing that answers questions about the device — a second reader of these HAL properties is a second place a future change can forget "presence is not usability"
fix: ask AudioDiagnostics instead of the HAL directly — add the property it should expose there and call that, rather than reading the property in a second place

failureMessage: a listener exposes the laugh log to whatever can reach the port — reintroducing one is a decision about who may read the room, not a feature
fix: drop the listener; a dashboard, metrics port or remote-control API needs the owner's sign-off, a loopback-only default and an auth/CSRF story in RULES.md first
